text.p: The boss of Oracle Corp, rumoured to about to bid for Apple computers, said on Thursday that Apple would make a great supplier of the new stripped-down, low-cost network computers (NCs).

Oracle Corp chief executive officer Larry Ellison, a major promoter of the new NCs that can access the Internet, made the comment about Apple Computer Inc amid mounting industry speculation that he would soon bid for Apple. His aim would be to turn it into an NC manufacturer with the Macintosh brand.
Asked whether he would personally make a bid for Apple, the software billionaire said he did not want to comment, but added: "Apple would be a great supplier of NCs."
Ellison was speaking at the Oracle OpenWorld 1997 business fair in Tokyo.
In late March, Ellison said he had formed an independent investor group to gauge interest in taking over the ailing computer maker.
Ellison said at that time that he would soon decide whether to make a bid based on the reaction from Apple investors, but he added that any bid would be independent of Oracle.

The move, which was not the first time Ellison had raised the possibility of personally leading a bid for Apple, came as the computer maker was struggling to recapture a profitable role in the intensely competitive personal computer industry.
Ellison has said for two years that he would like to buy Apple with his own money, partly to prevent Microsoft Corp from dominating the computer industry.

Apple, with its huge following of Macintosh fans, could be a key weapon. Apple has suffered declining market share for its famous brand of easy-to-use computers and endured several rounds of restructuring in recent years.

Oracle was the top vendor in the global database market in 1996 with a 30 percent market share, according to a recent study by Dataquest, a market research firm. Dataquest said Oracle posted 1996 database revenues of $1.70 billion.
